overall_reason: The work tabs ("Club night") wipe in the next example site with a clip-path over 520 to 820 ms, a showpiece where the picture is the content, so the sweep's 750 ms duration hit there is fitting, and the page uses named tokens (--ease-out-expo, --t-enter 0.9 s, --t-stagger 70 ms); but the hero stacks a word-by-word heading drop, a sunrise glow, a 16 s breathing loop and a pill rise, and 87 blocks are set to rise 28 px over 900 ms as they enter.

score.reason: T-PURPOSE and T-MOTION-SYSTEM pass for the tab showpiece and the token system, but T-CHOREOGRAPHY finds an entrance on every block and T-MOTION-BUDGET finds five hero entrances plus two loops.

findings.title: The page arrives once and is never gated
findings.where: every section block with [data-enter] (87 elements, for example the h2 "Design sense, packaged as a skill", "Sponsored by", "How it works"), 1440
findings.evidence: 87 elements declare "opacity, transform 900ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)" and the stylesheet hides "[data-enter]:not([data-entered])" at opacity 0 with a 28 px translate (--rise: 28px, --t-enter: .9s, --t-stagger: 70ms) until they enter. ROB-001 already records 81% of text hidden if the observer never fires.
findings.before: Headings, paragraphs and lists all rise 28 px over 900 ms as they come into view.
findings.after: Let the page arrive once at the hero and show the sections without a per-block entrance.
findings.why: The same rise on every block slows reading on each scroll and is the generated reveal pattern.

findings.title: Motion has a budget per page
findings.evidence: At load the hero runs hero-word on 7 words (950 ms each, dropping from 112% with a 7 degree turn), hero-rise on 3 blocks (800 ms), hero-rise-pill (700 ms), hero-sunrise on the glow (1400 ms) and hero-work-arrive on the preview (1200 ms), then hero-breathe, a 16 s infinite alternating drift and scale on the glow, plus a 22 s ember loop.
findings.before: Five load entrances and two loops in the first screen.
findings.after: Keep one arrival (the heading or the work preview) and hold the glow still.
findings.why: Several entrances plus a breathing glow pull attention away from the install command and the example tabs.

findings.title: Loops show a state or real data
findings.evidence: The glow runs "hero-breathe 16s ease-in-out infinite alternate" (opacity to 0.86, translate 2.5% -4%, scale 1.08) and its ::after runs "hero-ember 22s infinite alternate".
findings.before: The background glow drifts and pulses for as long as the page is open.
findings.after: Hold the glow still after the sunrise.
findings.why: The loop shows no state or data; it is slow, but it keeps a large area behind the headline moving.

strengths: The "Club night" tab swap is a clip-path wipe (520 ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), with scale and translate at 820 ms) where the example site is the content, and under reduced motion it swaps instantly (move 0 px).
Named motion tokens (--ease-out-expo, --ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.65, 0, .35, 1), --t-enter, --t-stagger) and 15 prefers-reduced-motion rules, which drop the rise and keep a 0.3 s opacity change.
